first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that simplifying onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Promotional pricing directly addresses competitive pressure but has documented 30-day retention harm, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Verify the strongest onboarding evidence and the pricing downside before committing; measure qualified activation and retain downstream retention and revenue guardrails.

final.rationale: Run a segmented onboarding-simplification experiment only for simple self-serve accounts, explicitly excluding complex-workspace accounts. The verified evidence directly addresses the current onboarding and activation declines, with completion up 13% and time-to-value improving by 2.1 days in the prior test. Track qualified activation, 60-day churn, and cohort revenue as guardrails. Do not pursue promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because verified gains came with a 12% retention decline and failure at first renewal.
